def _git_build_script(git_url: str, git_ref: str, image: str) -> str:
    ref = git_ref or "main"
    return f"""#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the coworking image from its repository.
#
# The repository is the source of truth of the recipe; this script clones the
# requested ref and runs the docker build the repository ships.
set -euo pipefail

REPO="{git_url}"
IMAGE="{image}"

workdir="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$workdir"' EXIT

git clone --depth 1 --branch "{ref}" "$REPO" "$workdir/repo"
docker build -t "$IMAGE" "$workdir/repo"
echo "Built $IMAGE from $REPO@{ref}"
"""


def _readme_template(item: CoworkingImage) -> str:
    lines = [
        f"# {item.name}",
        "",
        item.description or "Custom desktop image of the coworking gallery.",
        "",
        "| Field | Value |",
        "| --- | --- |",
        f"| Id | `{item.id}` |",
        f"| Source | `{item.source}` |",
        f"| Visibility | `{item.visibility}`"
        + (f" ({', '.join(item.projects)})" if item.projects else ""),
        "| Base image | `{}` |".format(item.base_image or "-"),
        "| Docker Hub | `{}` |".format(item.docker_ref or "-"),
        "| Repository | `{}` |".format(item.git_url or "-"),
        "| Tags | {} |".format(", ".join(f"`{tag}`" for tag in item.tags) or "-"),
        f"| Owner | `{item.created_by or '-'}` |",
        f"| Status | `{item.status}` |",
        "",
        "## Files",
        "",
        f"* `{MANIFEST_FILE}` — this definition, read by codx-junior.",
        f"* `{item.dockerfile}` — build recipe of the image.",
    ]
    if item.build_script:
        lines.append(f"* `{item.build_script}` — clone + build helper of the repository.")
    lines += [
        f"* `{SUPPORT_FOLDER}/` — files copied into the image.",
        f"* `{MEDIA_FOLDER}/` — icon and preview shown in the gallery.",
        "",
        "## Build",
        "",
        "```bash",
        f"docker build -t {item.docker_image()} .",
        "```",
        "",
        "Hand the folder to the `codx-junior-max` assistant to complete the recipe:",
        "",
        "```text",
        item.assistant_prompt,
        "```",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Visibility
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def visible_to(
    item: CoworkingImage,
    username: Optional[str] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    is_admin: bool = False,
) -> bool:
    """Whether a user of ``project_id`` may see this image in the gallery."""
    if is_admin:
        return True
    visibility = (item.visibility or "project").lower()
    if visibility == "global":
        return True
    if visibility == "user":
        return bool(username) and item.created_by == username
    if visibility == "custom":
        return bool(project_id) and project_id in (item.projects or [])
    return bool(project_id) and item.project_id == project_id


def can_edit(
    item: CoworkingImage,
    username: Optional[str] = None,
    project_id: Optional[str] = None,
    is_admin: bool = False,
) -> bool:
    """Owner, project admin role and global entries: see the API router."""
    if is_admin:
        return True
    if item.created_by and item.created_by == username:
        return True
    if (item.visibility or "project").lower() == "user":
        return False
    return bool(project_id) and item.project_id == project_id


def build_prompt(item: CoworkingImage, folder_path: str) -> str:
    """Instruction that hands the folder to the ``codx-junior-max`` assistant."""
    origin = {
        "dockerfile": f"base image `{item.base_image or DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE}`",
        "dockerhub": f"Docker Hub reference `{item.docker_ref}`",
        "git": f"repository `{item.git_url}` (ref `{item.git_ref or 'main'}`)",
    }.get(item.source, f"source `{item.source}`")
    return (
        f"As the `{ASSISTANT_PROFILE}` assistant, create the coworking desktop image "
        f"**{item.name}** in the folder "
        f"`{os.path.join(folder_path, MANIFEST_FILE)}` (definition) and "
        f"`{os.path.join(folder_path, item.dockerfile)}` (recipe).\n\n"
        f"* Source: {origin}.\n"
        f"* Purpose: {item.description or 'custom desktop image for the team'}.\n"
        f"* Tags: {', '.join(item.tags) or 'none'}.\n"
        f"* Live view: port {item.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT}, desktop user "
        f"`{item.desktop_user}`.\n\n"
        "Steps:\n"
        "1. Complete the Dockerfile (packages, support files, entrypoint) keeping "
        "the live-view service of the base desktop working.\n"
        "2. Add the support files under `support/` and the gallery icon/preview "
        f"under `{MEDIA_FOLDER}/`; list them in `{MANIFEST_FILE}` "
        "(media, support_files, icon_url, screenshot_url).\n"
        "3. Build the image and smoke-test that the desktop starts.\n"
        f"4. Set `status` to `ready` (or `error` with the message) in `{MANIFEST_FILE}`.\n"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Library
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class CoworkingImageLibrary:
    """Filesystem-backed gallery of custom coworking images."""

    def __init__(self, codx_path: str, project_id: Optional[str] = None, project_name: Optional[str] = None):
        self.codx_path = codx_path
        self.project_id = project_id
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.root = os.path.join(codx_path, COWORKING_FOLDER, IMAGES_FOLDER)
        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)

    # ── paths ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def folder_name(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> str:
        """``<image_id>.<slug>``: a stable, human-readable folder name."""
        return f"{item.id}.{item.slug}"

    def folder_path(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        if not image_id:
            return None
        for folder in Path(self.root).iterdir():
            if not folder.is_dir() or folder.name == ".trash":
                continue
            if folder.name == image_id or folder.name.split(".")[0] == image_id:
                if os.path.isfile(str(folder / MANIFEST_FILE)):
                    return str(folder)
        return None

    def file_path(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str) -> str:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            raise FileNotFoundError(image_id)
        return os.path.join(folder, _safe_relative(relative_path))

    # ── CRUD ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def list(self) -> List[CoworkingImage]:
        items: List[CoworkingImage] = []
        if not os.path.isdir(self.root):
            return items
        for folder in Path(self.root).iterdir():
            if not folder.is_dir() or folder.name == ".trash":
                continue
            item = self._read(str(folder / MANIFEST_FILE))
            if item:
                items.append(item)
        items.sort(key=lambda entry: entry.updated_at or entry.created_at or "", reverse=True)
        return items

    def list_visible(
        self,
        username: Optional[str] = None,
        project_id: Optional[str] = None,
        is_admin: bool = False,
        q: Optional[str] = None,
        visibility: Optional[str] = None,
        tag: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> List[CoworkingImage]:
        needle = (q or "").strip().lower()
        wanted_tag = (tag or "").strip().lower()
        wanted_visibility = (visibility or "").strip().lower()
        result = []
        for item in self.list():
            if not visible_to(item, username=username, project_id=project_id, is_admin=is_admin):
                continue
            if wanted_visibility and item.visibility != wanted_visibility:
                continue
            if wanted_tag and wanted_tag not in [entry.lower() for entry in item.tags]:
                continue
            if needle:
                haystack = " ".join(
                    [item.name, item.description, item.slug, " ".join(item.tags), item.docker_ref or "", item.git_url or ""]
                ).lower()
                if needle not in haystack:
                    continue
            result.append(item)
        return result

    def get(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        if not image_id:
            return None
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        return self._read(os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE)) if folder else None

    def save(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> CoworkingImage:
        folder = os.path.join(self.root, self.folder_name(item))
        os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
        for name in (SUPPORT_FOLDER, MEDIA_FOLDER):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(folder, name), exist_ok=True)
        item.folder = os.path.basename(folder)
        item.updated_at = _now()
        stored = item.model_copy(update={"assistant_prompt": ""})
        tmp = os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE + ".tmp")
        with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            json.dump(stored.to_dict(), handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
        os.replace(tmp, os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE))
        try:
            os.chmod(os.path.join(folder, MANIFEST_FILE), MANIFEST_MODE)
        except OSError:
            pass
        item.assistant_prompt = build_prompt(item, folder)
        return item

    def delete(self, image_id: str) -> bool:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            return False
        shutil.rmtree(folder, ignore_errors=True)
        return True

    # ── creation / import ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def create(
        self,
        req: CreateCoworkingImageRequest,
        created_by: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> CoworkingImage:
        name = (req.name or "").strip()
        if not name:
            raise ValueError("The image needs a name")
        source = (req.source or "dockerfile").strip().lower()
        if source not in SOURCES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown source '{req.source}'. Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCES)}")
        visibility = (req.visibility or "project").strip().lower()
        if visibility not in VISIBILITIES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown visibility '{req.visibility}'. Use one of: {', '.join(VISIBILITIES)}")
        projects = [entry.strip() for entry in (req.projects or []) if entry and entry.strip()]
        if visibility == "custom" and not projects:
            raise ValueError("visibility=custom needs at least one project")
        if source == "dockerhub" and not (req.docker_ref or "").strip():
            raise ValueError("A Docker Hub import needs the image reference")
        if source == "git" and not (req.git_url or "").strip():
            raise ValueError("A repository import needs the git URL")

        slug = _slug(name)
        item = CoworkingImage(
            id=uuid.uuid4().hex[:8],
            slug=slug,
            name=name,
            description=(req.description or "").strip(),
            source=source,
            base_image=(req.base_image or "").strip() or (
                (req.docker_ref or "").strip() if source == "dockerhub" else DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE
            ),
            docker_ref=(req.docker_ref or "").strip() or None,
            git_url=(req.git_url or "").strip() or None,
            git_ref=(req.git_ref or "").strip() or None,
            media=[entry for entry in (req.media or []) if entry],
            icon_url=req.icon_url or None,
            screenshot_url=req.screenshot_url or None,
            tags=[entry for entry in (req.tags or []) if entry],
            visibility=visibility,
            projects=projects,
            created_by=created_by,
            project_id=self.project_id,
            project_name=self.project_name,
            created_at=_now(),
            updated_at=_now(),
            status="draft",
            live_port=req.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT,
        )
        self.save(item)
        if req.scaffold:
            self._scaffold(item)
        return self.get(item.id) or item

    def _scaffold(self, item: CoworkingImage) -> None:
        """Write the starter files; safe to call twice (never overwrites)."""
        folder = self.folder_path(item.id)
        if not folder:
            return
        dockerfile = os.path.join(folder, getattr(item, "dockerfile", DOCKERFILE_FILE))
        if not os.path.exists(dockerfile):
            if item.source == "dockerhub":
                content = _dockerhub_dockerfile(item.docker_ref or item.base_image or "", item.name, item.slug)
            else:
                content = _dockerfile_template(
                    item.name,
                    item.description,
                    item.base_image or DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE,
                    item.desktop_user,
                    item.live_port or DEFAULT_LIVE_PORT,
                    item.slug,
                )
            _write_file(dockerfile, content)
        if item.source == "git" and item.git_url:
            script = os.path.join(folder, BUILD_SCRIPT)
            if not os.path.exists(script):
                _write_file(
                    script,
                    _git_build_script(item.git_url, item.git_ref or "main", item.docker_image()),
                    executable=True,
                )
            item.build_script = BUILD_SCRIPT
        item.support_files = sorted(
            {
                entry.path
                for entry in self.files(item.id)
                if not entry.is_manifest and entry.path != README_FILE
            }
        )
        self.save(item)
        _write_file(os.path.join(folder, README_FILE), _readme_template(item))

    def import_from_dockerhub(self, reference: str, created_by: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs: Any) -> CoworkingImage:
        """Import an existing Docker Hub image as a coworking image."""
        reference = (reference or "").strip()
        if not reference:
            raise ValueError("A Docker Hub reference is required")
        name = kwargs.pop("name", None) or reference.split(":")[0].split("/")[-1]
        req = CreateCoworkingImageRequest(
            name=name,
            source="dockerhub",
            docker_ref=reference,
            description=kwargs.pop("description", None) or f"Imported from Docker Hub: {reference}",
            tags=kwargs.pop("tags", []) or ["imported", "dockerhub"],
            **kwargs,
        )
        return self.create(req, created_by=created_by)

    def import_from_git(self, git_url: str, created_by: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs: Any) -> CoworkingImage:
        """Import a repository that already ships a Dockerfile."""
        git_url = (git_url or "").strip()
        if not git_url:
            raise ValueError("A repository URL is required")
        name = kwargs.pop("name", None) or git_url.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1].removesuffix(".git")
        req = CreateCoworkingImageRequest(
            name=name,
            source="git",
            git_url=git_url,
            git_ref=kwargs.pop("git_ref", None) or "main",
            description=kwargs.pop("description", None) or f"Imported from repository: {git_url}",
            tags=kwargs.pop("tags", []) or ["imported", "git"],
            **kwargs,
        )
        return self.create(req, created_by=created_by)

    def update(self, image_id: str, req: UpdateCoworkingImageRequest) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        item = self.get(image_id)
        if not item:
            return None
        changes = req.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        if "visibility" in changes:
            visibility = str(changes["visibility"]).strip().lower()
            if visibility not in VISIBILITIES:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown visibility '{visibility}'. Use one of: {', '.join(VISIBILITIES)}")
            changes["visibility"] = visibility
        if "source" in changes:
            source = str(changes["source"]).strip().lower()
            if source not in SOURCES:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown source '{source}'. Use one of: {', '.join(SOURCES)}")
            changes["source"] = source
        if "name" in changes and changes["name"]:
            item.slug = _slug(str(changes["name"]), item.slug)
        updated = item.model_copy(update=changes)
        if updated.visibility == "custom" and not updated.projects:
            raise ValueError("visibility=custom needs at least one project")
        return self.save(updated)

    # ── files ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    def files(self, image_id: str) -> List[ImageFileInfo]:
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not folder:
            return []
        result: List[ImageFileInfo] = []
        for path in sorted(Path(folder).rglob("*")):
            if not path.is_file() or path.name.endswith(".tmp"):
                continue
            relative = str(path.relative_to(folder)).replace(os.sep, "/")
            result.append(
                ImageFileInfo(
                    path=relative,
                    size=path.stat().st_size,
                    is_manifest=relative == MANIFEST_FILE,
                )
            )
        return result

    def read_file(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str) -> ImageFileContent:
        path = self.file_path(image_id, relative_path)
        if not os.path.isfile(path):
            raise FileNotFoundError(relative_path)
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
            return ImageFileContent(path=_safe_relative(relative_path), content=handle.read())

    def write_file(self, image_id: str, relative_path: str, content: str) -> ImageFileContent:
        path = self.file_path(image_id, relative_path)
        _write_file(path, content, executable=path.endswith(".sh"))
        item = self.get(image_id)
        if item:
            item.support_files = sorted(
                {entry.path for entry in self.files(image_id) if not entry.is_manifest and entry.path != README_FILE}
            )
            self.save(item)
        return ImageFileContent(path=_safe_relative(relative_path), content=content)

    def prompt_for(self, image_id: str) -> Optional[str]:
        item = self.get(image_id)
        folder = self.folder_path(image_id)
        if not item or not folder:
            return None
        return build_prompt(item, folder)

    # ── internals ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    @staticmethod
    def _read(path: str) -> Optional[CoworkingImage]:
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
                item = CoworkingImage(**json.load(handle))
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return None
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - corrupt manifest
            logger.warning("Could not read coworking image '%s': %s", path, ex)
            return None
        item.folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
        item.assistant_prompt = build_prompt(item, os.path.dirname(path))
        return item


def _write_file(path: str, content: str, executable: bool = False) -> None:
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(content)
    if executable:
        try:
            os.chmod(path, 0o755)
        except OSError:
            pass


def coworking_image_library(settings: Any) -> CoworkingImageLibrary:
    """Return the gallery of the project behind ``settings``."""
    return CoworkingImageLibrary(
        codx_path=settings.codx_path,
        project_id=getattr(settings, "project_id", None),
        project_name=getattr(settings, "project_name", None),
    )

```py api/codx/junior/runtime.py
"""
Ephemeral runtime folders shared by the platform subsystems.

``<project>/.codx`` is *durable* state: project settings, profiles and task
cards a human edits. Everything the platform writes while it runs — locks,
worker heartbeats, atomic temp files and rebuildable caches such as the project
atlas or the dependency graph — must not land there, otherwise the repository
working tree churns on its own and every ``git status`` is noise.

Those files live in a runtime folder instead::

    <CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH>/<project-slug>-<hash>/
        atlas/atlas.db
        board_manager/{worker.json,.state.lock,locks/}
        orchestration/{worker.json,locks/}
        dependency_graph.json
        domain_map.json
        project_summary.md
        wiki_settings.json

The folder is expendable: removing it only costs a rebuild. Its location is
``CODX_JUNIOR_RUNTIME_PATH`` (default ``<tmp>/codx-junior-runtime``, so ``/tmp``
on Linux) because nothing there has to survive a restart.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os

from codx.junior.globals import RUNTIME_FOLDER

#: Generated wiki category index (source file -> wiki page mapping).
WIKI_SETTINGS_FILE = "wiki_settings.json"


def project_runtime_dir(codx_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the runtime folder of the project owning ``codx_path``.

    The name is human readable (project folder name plus a short hash of the
    absolute ``codx_path``) so two projects sharing a folder name never collide.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> project_runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e'
    """
    return os.path.join(RUNTIME_FOLDER, _project_slug(codx_path))


def runtime_dir(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return (creating it) a folder inside the project's runtime folder.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_dir("/projects/app/.codx", "board_manager")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/board_manager'
    """
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *[p for p in parts if p])
    os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def runtime_file(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return a file path inside the project's runtime folder.

    The parent folder is created when ``parts`` has more than one element, so
    callers can hand the path straight to ``open(..., "a")`` or to a lock
    helper without extra bookkeeping.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> runtime_file("/projects/app/.codx", "atlas", "atlas.db")
        '/tmp/codx-junior-runtime/app-1a2b3c4d5e/atlas/atlas.db'
    """
    parts = [p for p in parts if p]
    path = os.path.join(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), *parts)
    if len(parts) > 1:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    else:
        os.makedirs(project_runtime_dir(codx_path), exist_ok=True)
    return path


# ── Generated data plane ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# ``.codx`` holds two very different things:
#
# * **Shared artifacts** a human edits and the team shares through git: profiles,
#   task cards, boards, teams, workspaces. These stay tracked.
# * **The data plane**: everything the platform generates while it runs — chat
#   turn records, browser sessions, the harness audit journal, orchestration and
#   board state, rebuildable indexes. It is unbounded, model-influenced and
#   *untrusted*, so it must never be committed: a single tool output that prints
#   a token would otherwise enter git history forever.
#
# The data plane is addressed through :func:`data_dir` / :func:`data_file` so it
# can be relocated OUTSIDE the repository with one environment variable, and so
# the ignore rules and the CISO repo check can be driven by one list
# (:data:`DATA_PLANE_ENTRIES`) instead of a hand-maintained copy.

#: Environment variable that moves the generated data plane outside the repo.
ENV_DATA_PATH = "CODX_JUNIOR_CODX_DATA_PATH"

#: Entries below ``.codx`` that belong to the generated data plane and are never
#: tracked by git. ``.gitignore`` mirrors this list and
#: ``api/tests/security/ciso_repo_check.py`` verifies both stay in sync.
DATA_PLANE_ENTRIES = (
    "chat_turns",
    "browser_sessions",
    "browser_downloads",
    "computer_downloads",
    "computer_library",
    "coworking",
    "harness",
    "orchestration",
    "board_manager",
    "autonomy",
    "atlas",
    "db",
    "logs",
    "media",
    "tmp",
    "cache",
    "dependency_graph.json",
    "domain_map.json",
    "project_summary.md",
    "wiki_settings.json",
)


def _project_slug(codx_path: str) -> str:
    """Return a filesystem-safe, collision-free name for a project."""
    absolute = os.path.abspath(str(codx_path or "."))
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(absolute)) or "project"
    safe = "".join(char if char.isalnum() or char in "-_." else "-" for char in name)
    digest = hashlib.sha1(absolute.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:10]
    return f"{safe}-{digest}"


def data_root(codx_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Return the root of the project's generated data plane.

    Defaults to the project's ``.codx`` folder, which keeps every existing
    install (and every bind mount that points inside it) working unchanged.
    Setting ``CODX_JUNIOR_CODX_DATA_PATH`` relocates the whole data plane to an
    external folder, one subfolder per project, so a deployment can keep
    generated runtime state completely outside the repository::

        CODX_JUNIOR_CODX_DATA_PATH=/var/lib/codx-junior/data
        >>> data_root("/projects/app/.codx")            # doctest: +SKIP
        '/var/lib/codx-junior/data/app-1a2b3c4d5e'
    """
    raw = str(codx_path or "").strip()
    override = (os.environ.get(ENV_DATA_PATH) or "").strip()
    if override:
        return os.path.join(
            os.path.abspath(os.path.expanduser(override)), _project_slug(raw or ".")
        )
    return os.path.abspath(raw) if raw else ""


def data_dir(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return (creating it) a folder of the generated data plane.

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> data_dir("/projects/app/.codx", "chat_turns")
        '/projects/app/.codx/chat_turns'
    """
    kept = [part for part in parts if part]
    path = os.path.join(data_root(codx_path), *kept) if kept else data_root(codx_path)
    if path:
        os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)
    return path


def data_file(codx_path: str, *parts: str) -> str:
    """
    Return a file path inside the generated data plane (parent created).

    Example (doctest: +SKIP):
        >>> data_file("/projects/app/.codx", "harness", "audit.jsonl")
        '/projects/app/.codx/harness/audit.jsonl'
    """
    kept = [part for part in parts if part]
    if not kept:
        return data_root(codx_path)
    path = os.path.join(data_root(codx_path), *kept) if data_root(codx_path) else os.path.join(*kept)
    parent = os.path.dirname(path)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    return path
```

Taking `max`. Three slices in one run. Reading the exact anchors first.Slice 3 first — the per-browser chat index in the store.Slice 1 — the file explorer modal.Slice 2 — compress `BrowserViewer` to a single header row.Slice 1+2+3 are written. The QA gate blocked — not on my code but on a pre-existing api failure set; details below, no hiding.

## What happened

- You asked for three things in the coworking session: browsable mounted volumes, 1-row header + 1-row footer, and a per-browser chat index in the chats store.
- All three are implemented. `max` tier, one run, six files.

## What I did

```js
toProjectPath(value) {
  const raw = String(value || '').trim()
  if (!raw || raw === '—') return null
  const base = this.absoluteProjectPath
  if (base && (raw === base || raw.startsWith(`${base}/`))) {
    return raw.slice(base.length).replace(/^\/+/, '')
  }
  // A plain "/docs" is the project-relative path the bind was created from;
  // "/home/<project>" is where the whole project lands inside the container.
  const home = this.homePath
  if (raw === home) return ''
  if (raw.startsWith(`${home}/`)) return raw.slice(home.length + 1)
  if (this.isVm && raw.startsWith('/shared')) {
    return raw.slice('/shared'.length).replace(/^\/+/, '')
  }
  return raw.replace(/^\/+/, '')
}
```

- **`BrowserSessionPanel.vue`** — footer is `flex-nowrap` with `py-1`; the timestamp/Live-view hide below `lg`/`xl` and the button labels below `md`, so it stays one row down to narrow docks. The **Folders** button opens the new modal through the global `<modal>` (re-parented to the app root, the same fix that made the Chat picker visible inside dockview panels).

## What happened

- The dead run had already written the pieces: `CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue` + `CoworkingFileBrowser.vue` + `volumeMappings.js` (new) and a `Folders` button inside the session footer — but its work was never verified, and your screenshot shows that footer **without** the button, so the page you were looking at was older than the code on disk.

Ruled out: compile error, wrong component, and the pytest failures (untouched `api/`).

## What I did

- Re-verified the module still compiles (200). No other file touched.

## Demo

Hard-reload `https://gbrian.codxjunior.com` (Ctrl+Shift+R) → open a coworking session → footer → **Mapped folders**.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — if the button is still missing after the hard reload, I check the HMR socket/`optimizeDeps` (lodash errors in the client log) and restart the client container.
- `quick` — remember the last browsed folder per session instead of resetting to the first bind.
- `max` — remove the second strip above the footer (the `cxj` / connectors status of the chat pane) so the bottom is one row also when the chat is open.

- Rewrote `client/src/components/browsers/volumeMappings.js`: `reportedMounts()` now consumes `shared_folders[]` (project-relative `folder` + `mount_path`) and adds the downloads bind only when no share already covers it; docker-inspect style binds kept as fallback.

```py api/codx/junior/browser/model.py
class SharedFolder(BaseModel):
    """
    One host folder bind mounted inside a browser container.

    ``folder`` is the project-relative path (``""`` means the project itself),
    ``host_path`` the absolute host folder and ``mount_path`` the path the same
    folder gets inside the container (``/home/<project_name>/<folder>`` unless
    the caller asked for a custom mount point).
    """

    id: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Immutable share identifier (auto-generated)"
    )
    name: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Human-readable label of the shared folder"
    )
    folder: Optional[str] = Field(
        default=None,
        description="Project-relative folder ('' or None means the project root)"
    )
    host_path: str = Field(
        description="Absolute host folder bind mounted into the container"
    )
    mount_path: str = Field(
        description="Path of the folder inside the container (e.g. /home/proj/docs)"
    )
    readonly: bool = Field(
        default=False,
        description="Mount the folder read-only (the browser cannot write into it)"
    )

    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        if not self.id:
            self.id = str(uuid4())

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert the share to a dictionary for JSON serialization."""
        return self.model_dump(exclude_none=False)

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> "SharedFolder":
        """Reconstruct a share from a dictionary."""
        return SharedFolder(**data)

    def contains(self, host_path: str) -> bool:
        """Return True when *host_path* lives inside this shared folder."""
        base = os.path.abspath(self.host_path)
        target = os.path.abspath(host_path or "")
        return target == base or target.startswith(base + os.sep)

    def container_path(self, relative_path: str = "") -> str:
        """
        Return the container path of a file inside this share.

        Args:
            relative_path: Path relative to the shared folder.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When the path escapes the shared folder.
        """
        base = (self.mount_path or "").rstrip("/")
        relative = (relative_path or "").strip().strip("/")
        if not relative:
            return base
        parts = [part for part in relative.split("/") if part not in ("", ".")]
        if any(part == ".." for part in parts):
            raise ValueError(f"'{relative_path}' is outside the shared folder")
        return f"{base}/{'/'.join(parts)}"

    def file_url(self, relative_path: str = "") -> str:
        """Return the ``file://`` URL the browser must open for a shared file."""
        return f"file://{self.container_path(relative_path)}"

    def file_path(self, relative_path: str = "") -> str:
        """
        Return the host path of a file inside this share.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When the path escapes the shared folder.
        """
        base = os.path.abspath(self.host_path)
        relative = (relative_path or "").strip().lstrip("/")
        target = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(base, relative)) if relative else base
        if target != base and not target.startswith(base + os.sep):
            raise ValueError(f"'{relative_path}' is outside the shared folder")
        return target

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"SharedFolder(name={self.name!r}, {self.host_path} -> {self.mount_path})"
```

The folder icon now opens the real **FileExplorer** (same component the Files app uses), not my inline table.

## What happened

- The "Mapped folders" modal listed the binds but browsed them with a read-only inline listing I had written, so files could be seen as a list but not worked with.
- You asked for the project's FileExplorer to open the folder.

## What I did

- `client/src/components/browsers/CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue` rewritten: the chip row stays (one per mounted bind from `shared_folders[]`), and the body is now `<FileExplorer :root-path="...">` rooted at the **absolute** path of the selected bind (`abs_project_path/<folder>`), so it can never walk above the mount.
- Clicking a file no longer dies: FileExplorer emits an absolute path, I fold it to project-relative and render `<FileViewer :params="{filePath}">` inside the same dialog, with a **Back to files** button — read/edit/download without losing the modal.
- The old `CoworkingFileBrowser` is now only used by the volume-mappings modal (unchanged).
- Validation: Vite transform returns **200** for the component; `qa_review_changes` on that file → `require_approval`, 1 finding, `missing-tests` (medium, no client test harness for these components — nothing else).

## Demo

Hard-reload → coworking session → footer **Mapped folders** → pick a folder chip → the FileExplorer toolbar (new file/folder, upload, rename, delete) is there → click a file to open it.

## Next tasks

- `quick` — apply the same FileExplorer to `CoworkingVolumeExplorer` (the volume table's own "Files" action still uses the old inline body).
- `quick` — start the explorer on the bind that matches the volume you clicked in the table instead of always the first one.
- `max` — QA explorer pass at ~900px width: confirm modal height, `Esc`/close behaviour and that a save from FileViewer refreshes the listing.

messages.content: Cool, now is working but we need to fix how file explorer fits in the dialog

Root cause is clear: the dialog box is capped at `max-w-2xl` (42rem) but the browser root demanded `md:w-[60rem]`, so the FileExplorer toolbar was painted outside the dialog and clipped. Fixing the fit on both sides.Found the fit bug: the dialog box is capped at `max-w-2xl` (42rem ≈ 672px) but my browser root asked for `md:w-[60rem]` (960px), so the FileExplorer toolbar was laid out wider than the dialog and painted outside it — that's the filter input cut at the border.

## What happened

- The mapped-folders modal showed the FileExplorer, but its content overflowed the dialog: the toolbar row extended past the right edge and the filter field was clipped.
- Cause: fixed 60rem width on the browser root vs `max-w-2xl` on the global `<modal>`, plus two `flex-1` children in the FileExplorer toolbar with no `min-w-0` (a long breadcrumb can't shrink, so it pushes the row wider).

## What I did

- `CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue`: root is now `w-full max-w-full h-[70vh] max-h-[70vh] overflow-hidden` (no more 60rem/85vw), and the explorer frame got `min-w-0` — it fits the dialog instead of overflowing it, vertically bounded so the modal body never double-scrolls.
- `FileExplorer.vue`: toolbar row + breadcrumb + search-input wrapper gained `min-w-0`, so the breadcrumb scrolls/truncates and the filter input shrinks inside the dialog (no behaviour change in the Files app).
- `FileViewer.vue`: header row got `min-w-0 overflow-hidden` so a long file name/size/date can't widen the dialog when a file is opened from the browser.
- Validated: the live Vite server transforms all three modules (`200`); `qa_review_changes` → `require_approval`, 4 medium findings, all `missing-tests`/coverage (no client test harness for these components — named under Next tasks).

- `quick` — unit test for `volumeMappings.js` + a component test for `CoworkingFoldersBrowser.vue` (clears 3 of the 4 gate findings).

messages.content: How can I make sure that the chat is connected with the browser I'm seeing?

## What happened

- You asked how to prove the chat in the right pane is the one bound to the browser on the left (`Linkedin post` / `browser_fc22d9cf`).
- Answer: the link is by **id**, and there are four checkable signals in the UI — the badge alone is not proof, the session name/id pair is.

## What I did

- Checked the wiring (no code changed):
  - `BrowserSessionPanel` renders `BrowserViewer` (left) and `Chat` (right) from the **same object** `selectedSession`, and the chat is opened by id from `session.chat_ids` (`:chat="browserChat"`, line 1221). So pane and viewer cannot point at different sessions unless the chat id is stale.
  - The subtitle under the chat title is `selectedSession.name` (line 1118) — if the viewer header says `Linkedin post` **and** the chat subtitle says `Linkedin post`, they are the same session.
  - The `browser tools` badge (green, line 1193) means the chat's profiles include `browser`/`computer` (`browserChatHasTools`). Grey `AI` = it will answer but never drive the page.
  - The chat itself stores the session in `Chat.meta_data["browser"]` (`api/codx/junior/browser/model.py:10`); `session.chat_ids` / `controller_chat_id` record the reverse. Same id as the **Container** shown in Settings.
  - Footer `1 chat(s)` comes from `session.chat_ids.length` (line 74) — a second signal that the pane's session is the one listed.

- Rule of thumb: **green `browser tools` + matching session name above and below + the container id in Settings** = connected. If the badge is ghost, or the names differ, the chat is a plain chat with no browser.

## Demo

In that chat, ask: *"Which browser session and URL are you controlling?"* — the answer must name `browser_fc22d9cf` and the URL in the address bar on the left (`linkedin.com/company/85521582/admin/dashboard/`).

## Next tasks

- `quick` — show the session id in the chat pane subtitle (e.g. `Linkedin post · fc22d9cf`) so the connection is visible without opening Settings.
- `quick` — turn the badge into a real check: green only when `chat.meta_data["browser"] === selectedSession.id`, with a tooltip naming the mismatch when it is not.
- `max` — a "Reconnect" action in the chat menu that re-links the chat to the session you are looking at (`add_chat` on the new session, `remove_chat` on the old one).

**Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok` ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

## What happened

- The AI resolves its browser with `get_session_for_chat(chat_id)` = "first session whose `chat_ids` contains the chat" → with duplicates it is list-order dependent, so a chat opened on browser B could drive browser A. That is exactly what you hit.

  - `connect_chat` and `save_session_to_chat` call it, so linking a chat to a session **moves** it instead of sharing it (existing duplicates are repaired on the next open);

- `client/src/components/browsers/BrowserSessionPanel.vue` — after opening, `warnIfChatBoundElsewhere(chat)` compares `chat.meta_data.browser.id` with the panel session and raises an error notification when they differ, so a chat bound elsewhere is never driven silently.

```python
    def detach_chat(self, chat_id: str, keep_session_id: Optional[str] = None) -> List[str]:
        """
        Enforce the 1:1 chat ↔ session relation.

        A chat can drive exactly one co-desktop: every session other than

        from ``chat_ids`` and the control lease cleared when that chat held it).

        Args:
            chat_id: Chat being (re)bound.
            keep_session_id: Session that keeps/claims the chat.

        Returns:
            Ids of the sessions the chat was released from.
        """
        if not chat_id:
            return []
        released = []
        for session in self.list_sessions():
            if keep_session_id and session.id == keep_session_id:
                continue
            if not session.has_chat(chat_id):
                continue
            session.remove_chat(chat_id)
            if session.controller_chat_id == chat_id:
                session.controller_chat_id = None
            self._save_session_file(session)
            released.append(session.id)
            logger.info(
                "Chat %s released from session %s (a chat drives one co-desktop)",
                chat_id[:8], session.id[:8],
            )
        return released
```

```py api/codx/junior/browser/browser_manager.py
"""
BrowserManager / ComputerManager — CRUD and lifecycle for computer sessions.

A session is a machine shared by the user and the AI.  ``kind="browser"`` keeps
the original Chromium/CDP behaviour; ``linux`` runs a desktop container driven
through ``docker exec``; ``windows``/``macos`` run QEMU VMs driven through VNC;
``remote`` points at an existing VNC/SSH machine.  This class owns session
persistence, chat linking, activity audit, folder sharing and the per-session
runtime (BrowserRuntime for browsers, DesktopRuntime for desktops).

Follows the workspace pattern:
    .codx/browser_sessions/<session_id>/<session_id>.session

A session is created with a human-readable ``name`` and may be shared by several
chats (``session.chat_ids``).  The container is a Chromium instance with a live
VNC view (for the user) and a CDP endpoint (for the AI), so both actors control
the same browser page.

Folder sharing
--------------
Any number of project folders are mounted inside the browser container under a
single tree (``/home/<project_name>/<folder>``) and the browser downloads are
written inside a project folder, so the user and the AI exchange files with the
project instead of being locked in the container:

- ``configure_share`` decides the mounts when the session is created;
- the downloads folder is written into the browser profile *before* the container
  starts (``codx/junior/browser/download_settings.py``), because Chromium reads
  the download directory at launch — this is the durable half and covers the
  downloads the user starts in the live VNC view;
- the same folder is also applied through CDP on every connection
  (``Browser.setDownloadBehavior``), which is the live half: it also covers a
  download triggered by the AI while its connection is open;
- ``get_shared_paths`` / ``get_shared_files`` expose the mapping and the files
  the browser saved inside the project.

Browser window survival
-----------------------
Chromium exits when its last window (tab) is closed, while the container keeps
running: the live view stays up but the browser window is gone and the DevTools
endpoint is dead.  Two defences keep a session usable:

- a protected **keep-alive tab** is created with the session and ensured on every
  connection (``codx/junior/browser/tabs.py``), so closing every other tab leaves
  the window alive;
- ``connect_browser`` **recovers** a dead browser by restarting the container
  entrypoint (which relaunches Chromium with the mounted profile) and retrying
  the connection once.

Lifecycle primitives
--------------------
- ``create_session(name, chat_id, initial_url, description)`` : start a new container + persist metadata.
- ``stop_session(session_id)``      : stop the container but KEEP it (restartable).
- ``restart_session(session_id)``   : relaunch Chromium (recovery) / recreate a stopped session.
- ``delete_session(session_id)``    : stop the container, remove it and the folder.
- ``log_activity(...)``             : append an audit entry for a user/AI action.
"""
```
